# Page 1^page=1
Example in Oracle NEW CUSTOMER ( CustomerID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR2(100) ); ORDERS ( OrderID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, CustomerID NUMBER, OrderDate DATE, Amount NUMBER, FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES CUSTOMER(CustomerID) ); CUSTOMER: 100K tuples ORDERS: several million tuples EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT c.Name, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Amount FROM Customer c JOIN Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.CustomerID = 42;

# Page 2^page=2
Example in Oracle NEW CUSTOMER ( CustomerID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR2(100) ); ORDERS ( OrderID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, CustomerID NUMBER, OrderDate DATE, Amount NUMBER, FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES CUSTOMER(CustomerID) ); EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT c.Name, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Amount FROM Customer c JOIN Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.CustomerID = 42; Scan ORDERS Keep orders having CustomerID = 42 Find CustomerID = 42 in the index (primary key) Retrieve the CUSTOMER tuple Join the results Return SELECT result

# Page 3^page=3
Same Result, Different Access Paths NEW CUSTOMER ( CustomerID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR2(100) ); ORDERS ( OrderID NUMBER PRIMARY KEY, CustomerID NUMBER, OrderDate DATE, Amount NUMBER, FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES CUSTOMER(CustomerID) ); EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT c.Name, o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Amount FROM Customer c JOIN Orders o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.CustomerID = 42; CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customerON Orders(CustomerID); Find CustomerID = 42 in the ORDERS index (IDX_ORDERS_CUSTOMER) Retrieve the matching ORDERS tuples …

# Page 4^page=4
Query Formulation Matters! SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= DATE '2026-01-01’ AND OrderDate < DATE '2027-01-01'; SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM OrderDate) = 2026; CREATE INDEX idx_orders_dateON Orders(OrderDate); NEW

# Page 5^page=5
Also selectivity matters! SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= DATE '2026-01-01’ AND OrderDate < DATE '2027-01-01'; CREATE INDEX idx_orders_dateON Orders(OrderDate); NEW E.g., Oracle estimates that 80% of ORDERS satisfy the condition Good statistics → good cardinality estimates → potentially better execution plans
